description: When AWS/Azure/GCP have outages, correlating provider status with your alerts prevents wasted troubleshooting and supports customer communication.
value: Detecting cloud provider status and incident correlation early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Poll provider status APIs (e.g. status.aws.amazon.com, status.azure.com) or ingest RSS. Normalize to common schema. When your alerts spike, search status index for same time window and provider. Dashboard active incidents by provider.

knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud_status`.
• Install and configure Custom input (status page API or RSS), or status page integration with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Poll provider status APIs (e.g. status.aws.amazon.com, status.azure.com) or ingest RSS. Normalize to common schema. When your alerts spike, search status index for same time window and provider. Dashboard active incidents by provider.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud_status sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud_status sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" provider=* status=*impact*
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.13_cloud_provider_status_an_13"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=cloud_status` to detect cloud provider status and incident correlation. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_13_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (provider, service, status), Timeline (incidents), Single value (active incidents)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Custom input (status page API or RSS), or status page integration and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud provider status and incident correlation so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
